attributes.text: For each critical vendor: due diligence performed before onboarding
attributes.typical_evidence: Vendor security assessment questionnaire or SOC 2 report review records
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity requires pre-engagement security assessment of critical or high-risk vendors, and either complete dated vendor onboarding history through the test date proves that no critical or high-risk vendors were onboarded, or the most recent such vendor has pre-engagement security assessment records (questionnaire, SOC 2 review, or security evaluation). For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the pre-engagement security assessment requirement remains required. FAIL if critical or high-risk vendors can be onboarded with no due diligence process in place. A pre-engagement assessment process adopted after earlier critical or high-risk vendors were onboarded without it passes instead once it is adopted in writing with a date and its steps are in place, when every critical or high-risk vendor onboarded since adoption had the assessment before onboarding (or, where none has been onboarded since, complete dated vendor onboarding history shows none since the adoption date); the assessment names the earlier vendors and the adoption date. TYPE II (over the period): If no critical or high-risk vendors were onboarded in the period, complete dated vendor onboarding history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If such vendors were onboarded, PASS if every critical or high-risk vendor has a pre-engagement security assessment; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic onboarding without due diligence is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A two-person AI-native startup onboarded one critical payment vendor; no formal SOC 2 report was obtained, but the founder documented a short review note citing the vendor's published security attestation page before signing.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Compensating controls are a legitimate pass path at design stage, and for a solo/small team a documented review of a vendor's public attestation stands in for an unobtainable formal audit report. The basis is real and documented, so it passes on a proportional basis.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Vendor due diligence was adopted in writing on 1 September. The payment processor and the email provider were onboarded in March without it; the one critical vendor onboarded since, an AI provider, has a dated review of its SOC 2 report before onboarding, and the assessment names the two earlier vendors and the adoption date.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Due diligence adopted partway passes for readiness from its dated written adoption when every critical vendor onboarded since then was assessed first and the earlier ones are named.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The founder says new critical vendors have been reviewed first since September, but no written requirement or adoption date exists. The payment processor and the email provider were onboarded in March without a review, and no critical vendor has been onboarded since.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A stated practice is not a written, dated adoption, and the most recent critical vendor had no assessment before onboarding, so this is a gap. With a dated written requirement, its steps in place, complete dated vendor onboarding history showing no critical or high-risk vendor onboarded since the adoption date and the assessment naming the two March vendors and the adoption date, it would pass.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Vendor due diligence was adopted in writing on 1 September. The two March vendors were onboarded without it, and an AI provider onboarded in October was connected to production two weeks before its SOC 2 report was reviewed.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The most recent critical vendor, onboarded after adoption, was assessed only after onboarding, so the adoption route does not apply and the check is a gap.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual vendor security assessment questionnaire or SOC 2 report review records (not just a verbal description)? Or, for readiness and Type I, for a pre-engagement assessment process adopted after earlier critical or high-risk vendors were onboarded without it: does the evidence show its dated written adoption, its steps in place, and an assessment record for every such vendor onboarded since adoption (or complete dated onboarding history showing none since), with the earlier vendors and the adoption date named in the assessment?

Does the record show that due diligence was performed before onboarding? Or, under that adoption route, was every such vendor onboarded since adoption assessed before onboarding, or does complete dated onboarding history show none since the adoption date?

attributes.text: For each critical vendor: security posture assessed at least annually
attributes.typical_evidence: Annual vendor reassessment records or SOC 2 report review for current period
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity reassesses critical or high-risk vendors on a defined cycle (default: within the last 12 months), and either complete dated vendor inventory and access history through the test date proves that no such vendors exist, or the most recent reassessment record (SOC 2 report review, security questionnaire, or equivalent) falls within that cycle. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the defined periodic reassessment process remains required. FAIL if critical or high-risk vendors are used with no periodic reassessment process in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no critical or high-risk vendors existed in the period, complete dated vendor inventory and access history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. PASS if every critical or high-risk vendor has a reassessment within the defined cycle (default: within the last 12 months); isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of reassessment is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The last manual reassessment note for a critical vendor is 14 months old, but the entity uses an automated vendor-risk platform that continuously monitors that vendor's SOC 2 report expiry and would flag any lapse.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Compensating controls are a legitimate pass path: continuous automated monitoring of a vendor's certification status can stand in for a periodic manual reassessment when the basis is real and verifiable. The gap should not be called purely on the age of the last manual note.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual annual vendor reassessment records or soc 2 report review for current period (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that security posture assessed at least annually?

attributes.text: For each vendor with confidential data access: confidentiality commitments are signed
attributes.typical_evidence: Signed NDA or confidentiality clause in the vendor contract; for a vendor whose terms are accepted online, its business terms containing confidentiality commitments, with binding electronic execution evidenced by attributable acceptance of the governing terms, and evidence they cover the company's account
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity requires confidentiality commitments from vendors with access to confidential information, and the most recent such vendor has a signed NDA or confidentiality clause in their contract on file. If no vendor has access to confidential information as of the test date, complete dated vendor confidential-data access history through that date must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. This does not waive the confidentiality commitment process. FAIL if vendors can access confidential information with no confidentiality commitment process in place. TYPE II (over the period): PASS if every vendor with access to confidential information has signed confidentiality commitments on file; if no vendor had access to confidential information in the period, complete dated vendor confidential-data access history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of confidentiality commitments is a gap.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Confidentiality TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The vendor manager states verbally that the confidentiality NDA with a data-access vendor was signed, but no signed document or contract clause was pulled as evidence.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Verbal confirmation is never config or record evidence. The attribute requires an actual signed NDA or confidentiality clause on file, not an assertion that one exists.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual signed nda or confidentiality clause in vendor contract (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that confidentiality commitments are signed?

attributes.text: For each vendor with personal data access: privacy and data processing commitments are signed
attributes.typical_evidence: Signed DPA or privacy addendum in the vendor contract, or the vendor's DPA incorporated into its business terms, with binding electronic execution evidenced by attributable acceptance of the governing terms, and evidence the DPA covers the company's account and processing
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity requires privacy and data processing commitments from vendors with access to personal information, and the most recent such vendor has a signed DPA or privacy addendum on file. If no vendor has access to personal information as of the test date, complete dated vendor personal-data access history through that date must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. This does not waive the privacy and data processing commitment process. FAIL if vendors can access personal information with no data processing commitment process in place. TYPE II (over the period): PASS if every vendor with access to personal information has signed privacy commitments or a DPA on file; if no vendor had access to personal information in the period, complete dated vendor personal-data access history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of privacy commitments is a gap.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A data processing addendum for a vendor handling personal data is a Google Doc still marked 'DRAFT' with an unfilled signature block and no approval date.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A draft document is not an adopted or executed agreement. Draft banners and an empty signature block mean the commitment was never actually made, regardless of how complete the content looks.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual signed dpa or privacy addendum in vendor contract (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that privacy?
Does the record show that data processing commitments are signed?

attributes.text: Vendors whose controls your product depends on are identified and listed
attributes.typical_evidence: Vendor dependency list identifying which vendors' controls the product relies on
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: A document lists vendors whose controls the entity's product depends on (subservice organizations), with each vendor's relevant control areas identified. FAIL: No documented list of dependent vendors/subservice organizations.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The subservice organization list lives on an internal wiki page naming AWS and the payment processor with their control areas; the evidence captured is a screenshot of that live page rather than an exported file.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Live system screenshots are valid system evidence regardless of submission label. The page plainly identifies the dependent vendors and their control areas, satisfying the attribute.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a list of vendors whose controls the product depends on?
Are the dependent vendors named with their relevant control areas?

attributes.text: SOC 2 report, equivalent attestation, or a documented alternative assessment obtained for each dependent vendor
attributes.typical_evidence: SOC 2 Type II reports (or an equivalent attestation such as a SOC 3 or ISO 27001 certificate) on file for each dependent vendor (e.g., cloud providers, payment processors); for a vendor that offers no report, or whose report the entity has not obtained, a dated alternative assessment (a security questionnaire or a review of its published security documentation) with its conclusion
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: SOC 2 Type II reports (or equivalent attestation: a SOC 3, ISO 27001, SOC 1, etc.) are on file for each identified dependent vendor, or, for a dependent vendor that offers no such report, or whose report the entity has not obtained, a documented alternative assessment is on file (a completed security questionnaire, a review of the vendor's published security documentation, or controls the entity runs to cover the gap) that records the risks assessed, the conclusion and any responsibilities the entity carries itself. FAIL: Any dependent vendor has neither a SOC 2 report or equivalent attestation on file nor such a documented alternative assessment.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The cloud provider's public trust page states 'SOC 2 Type II certified,' and that page was accepted as the vendor's report without the actual PDF report being obtained or on file.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A provider's marketing or trust page is not this org's actual audit report, and accepting it records no risks, conclusion or responsibilities, so it is not a documented alternative assessment either. The check needs the report itself on file or, where the entity has not obtained it, a documented alternative assessment.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Two dependent vendors: the cloud provider's SOC 2 Type II report is on file; the email delivery vendor offers no SOC report or equivalent attestation, and a dated review of its published security documentation records the risks assessed, the conclusion and the controls the entity runs itself (it sends the vendor only non-sensitive notification text).
calibration_examples.reasoning: A dependent vendor that offers no report is covered by a documented alternative assessment recording the risks, the conclusion and the entity's own responsibilities.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The payment processor shares its SOC 2 report only under a mutual NDA the entity has not signed. The entity's dated review of the processor's published security documentation records the risks assessed, the conclusion and the controls the entity runs itself.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A documented alternative assessment covers a dependent vendor whose report the entity has not obtained.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show a SOC 2 report or equivalent attestation obtained for each dependent vendor, or, for a vendor that offers none or whose report the entity has not obtained, a documented alternative assessment with its conclusion?

attributes.text: Reports cover the examination period
attributes.typical_evidence: SOC 2 report cover pages showing report period, or bridge letters covering any gaps
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Each dependent vendor's SOC 2 report period overlaps with the entity's examination period, OR bridge letters cover any gap between the report period end and the examination period end. A vendor covered by a documented alternative assessment instead of a report (it offers none, or the entity has not obtained it) has no report period to test here. FAIL: Any dependent vendor's report period does not cover the examination period and no bridge letter covers the gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A dependent vendor's SOC 2 report period ended three months before the entity's examination period began, but a signed bridge letter from the vendor covers the intervening gap through the examination end date.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline: the pass criteria explicitly allow a bridge letter to cover a gap between report period and examination period, so this clause must not be skipped when it is present. The bridge letter satisfies coverage of the examination period.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: SOC 2 reports are on file for both dependent vendors. The cloud provider's report period runs through two months before the examination date. The payment processor's report period ended eight months before it, and no bridge letter covering the interval was requested or provided.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Holding a vendor's report is not the same as being covered for the period under examination, which is what this attribute tests. An eight month uncovered interval needs a bridge letter, and its absence leaves the entity relying on controls nobody has reported on for most of the period.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that reports cover the examination period (a vendor covered by a documented alternative assessment instead of a report has no report period to test)?

attributes.text: Reports are reviewed and vendor-operated controls are documented
attributes.typical_evidence: SOC 2 report review notes and documented vendor-operated controls; for a vendor covered by a documented alternative assessment instead of a report, that assessment
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: SOC 2 report review notes are on file for each dependent vendor, documenting any exceptions or modified opinions and listing vendor-operated controls relied upon; for a vendor covered by a documented alternative assessment instead of a report, the assessment stands in for the review notes when it records the conclusion and the vendor-operated controls relied upon. FAIL: No review notes for any dependent vendor's report, or vendor-operated controls are not documented.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The review of each vendor's SOC 2 report is recorded as a row in a shared tracker spreadsheet (vendor, reviewer, date, exceptions noted), with complementary user-entity controls listed in a separate onboarding doc rather than a single narrative memo.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes pass on the existence and use of the review process, not on the format or consolidation of its documentation. A tracker row plus a separate CSOC list together show the report was reviewed and vendor-operated controls documented.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that reports are reviewed (for a vendor covered by a documented alternative assessment instead of a report, that assessment with its conclusion)?
Does the evidence show that vendor-operated controls are documented?

attributes.text: Monitoring produces evidence of control operation (logs, dashboards, reports, or manual checklists)
attributes.typical_evidence: Monitoring dashboards, automated alerts, log-based reports, or manual checklists showing control operation
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: At least one monitoring output (dashboard, alert log, automated report, or manual checklist) with dated entries shows regular production of evidence of control operation, not ad hoc. FAIL: No monitoring outputs, or outputs are undated or produced ad hoc only.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A live screenshot of the company's cloud security dashboard, showing dated automated compliance-check results over the past quarter, was tagged generically as 'document' at intake rather than as a system capture.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Live system screenshots are system evidence regardless of how they were labeled at submission. Judge what the capture actually shows, dated, regularly produced monitoring output, not the intake tag it was filed under.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A weekly 'monitoring log' spreadsheet is manually typed by an employee, listing entries like 'checked dashboard, all good' with no attached screenshots, exports, or system-generated timestamps.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A client-authored spreadsheet is not system proof. Monitoring evidence needs an actual system output (dashboard capture, alert log, automated report) behind the claim, not a self-reported log describing that a check happened.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that monitoring produces evidence of control operation (logs, dashboards, reports, or manual checklists)?

attributes.text: Management reviewed security posture within the last year
attributes.typical_evidence: Management security review meeting records or security posture reports
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Management security posture review record (meeting notes, report, or documented review) is dated within the entity's defined review frequency period, and includes date and attendee/reviewer names. FAIL: No management security posture review record within the defined period, or record lacks date and attendees.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Management's quarterly security posture review happened on a recorded video call; the only record is a dated Slack thread summarizing the discussion with the two attendees named and key decisions listed.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: a dated Slack summary naming attendees and covering the substance of a security posture review satisfies this attribute even though it isn't a formal report document. Judge the content, not the medium.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that management reviewed security posture within the last {review_frequency} period?

attributes.text: Independent evaluation performed within the last year
attributes.typical_evidence: What counts, and all three are needed: someone who does not run your systems did the review; they wrote down what they looked at and what they found, with a date inside the last 12 months; and you wrote down what you did about it. A short review that meets all three counts. A long report that misses one does not. Where a small team can get one, easiest first: a partner-led cloud security review (an AWS, Azure or GCP partner firm, often free; the self-service review inside the cloud console is a self-assessment and does not count), a written review by a security person you know who does not build or run your systems, a small fixed-scope assessment by an independent security consultant, or a penetration test if a customer asks you for one anyway. A penetration test is not required. Chiaro cannot be your reviewer: the firm that would examine you cannot also be the independent one. Also accepted, where you hold the dated findings and your response: a customer's own security review of you, a completed prior examination report, an independent certification, or an internal audit report. Record why the reviewer is competent and why the route you chose fits you. This check does not have to close for readiness to finish.
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: An independent evaluation (internal audit, third-party assessment, or external auditor) of controls was performed within the last 12 months, by a party not responsible for the controls evaluated. FAIL: No independent evaluation within the last 12 months, or evaluation was performed by the same team responsible for the controls.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A 5-person startup has no internal audit function; instead, an independent third-party penetration testing firm performed a full assessment 8 months ago and delivered a dated report to leadership.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Compensating controls are a legitimate pass path at design stage: for a company this size, an independent external assessment stands in for a nonexistent internal audit function. Pass explicitly on this compensating basis.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Submitted as the independent evaluation: a thorough self assessment against the control list, dated four months ago, performed and signed by the engineering lead. That same person owns access provisioning, change management, and the monitoring configuration the assessment covers.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Independence in this attribute is about who performed the evaluation, not how rigorous it was, and a person cannot provide it over controls they operate. A careful self assessment is real evidence for management review, and that is a different attribute from this one.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A two-person startup on AWS submitted a Well-Architected Review report performed by a partner firm five months ago: security findings classified by risk, with a dated remediation plan the founders acted on.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The criterion asks for an independent evaluation of controls, not for any particular instrument. A partner-led cloud security review is a named party evaluating the control environment, with scope, dated findings, and a management response. It qualifies on the same basis a pen test would.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The founder ran an advanced AI security agent against their own repository and cloud account and submitted its forty-page findings export. No firm or individual signs the report; the tool subscription is in the founder's name.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Independence attaches to the party, not the tool. A tool run by the person responsible for the controls is a self-assessment however sophisticated the tool; an evaluation needs a named party who stands behind it and is not responsible for the controls evaluated.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Before signing, an enterprise customer's security team assessed the company's controls: the submission includes their dated questionnaire findings, a follow-up letter listing required fixes, and the company's written remediation responses.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A customer's security review is an independent party evaluating the control environment, and the captured artifact carries scope, findings, a date, and the management response. The unusual source does not matter; the substance of the evaluation does.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The managed IT provider that administers the company's endpoints, identity, and backups performed and signed an annual security review of that same environment, and the report is submitted as the independent evaluation.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The provider operates the controls it reviewed, so it is responsible for them and cannot independently evaluate them. Independence is about operational responsibility, not about being a separate legal entity.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A solo founder submits a written annual review of the company's controls performed by a technical advisor with a documented security background who holds advisory equity, operates none of the systems, and signed a dated report listing what was examined, three findings, and the founder's written responses.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Independence attaches to responsibility for the controls, not to the absence of any relationship, so an advisor who neither builds nor operates the systems can evaluate them. The report carries a named party, scope, dated findings, and a management response, which is the bar; weight it below a third-party assessment and record the competence basis in the file.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that independent evaluation performed within the last {review_frequency} period?

attributes.text: Process exists to identify and assess control deficiencies by severity
attributes.typical_evidence: Deficiency management procedure or control monitoring policy
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for identifying control deficiencies and assessing their severity (severity classification scheme defined). FAIL: No documented deficiency identification or severity assessment process.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company's incident response policy has a subsection defining deficiency severity levels (critical/high/medium/low) and triage criteria, but there is no standalone 'Deficiency Management Policy' document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: the attribute asks whether a documented process for identifying and rating deficiency severity exists, not that it live in a separately titled policy. Content embedded in a related policy satisfies the requirement.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a deficiency management procedure or control monitoring policy?

attributes.text: Process exists to communicate deficiencies to responsible parties and leadership
attributes.typical_evidence: Escalation procedure or deficiency reporting process documentation
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for communicating identified deficiencies to responsible parties and leadership, including escalation steps. FAIL: No documented deficiency communication or escalation process.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The engagement's internal risk policy has a clause stating identified control deficiencies must be reported to the CEO within 24 hours and to the board at the next scheduled meeting, but the clause sits inside a general 'Governance' section rather than a document titled for deficiency communication.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: a clear, documented escalation path with defined timing and named recipients satisfies this attribute regardless of which document section it appears in.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a escalation procedure or deficiency reporting process documentation?

attributes.text: Corrective action plans include assigned owners and timelines
attributes.typical_evidence: Corrective action plan template or tracker showing owner and timeline fields
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Corrective action plan template or tracker shows owner and timeline fields, and at least one example (if deficiencies have been identified) has both populated. FAIL: No corrective action tracking mechanism, or plans lack assigned owners or timelines.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The corrective action tracker template has 'Owner' and 'Due Date' columns, but the one populated example row shows Owner as 'TBD' and Due Date blank.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Structural existence of the right columns is not enough; the pass criteria require an actual example with both fields populated. An unassigned owner and missing timeline in the only real entry means the requirement is not met in practice.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that corrective action plans include assigned owners?
Does the evidence show that timelines?

attributes.text: For each deficiency (if any): remediation is tracked to completion
attributes.typical_evidence: Deficiency tracker showing progress and closure records
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity tracks identified deficiencies to completion, and the most recent deficiency has a tracker entry showing progress through completion with timestamps. If no deficiencies were identified, complete dated source history must prove zero events; record non-occurrence. FAIL if deficiencies can be identified with no remediation tracking process in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no deficiencies were identified, complete dated source history must prove zero events; record non-occurrence. If deficiencies were identified, PASS if every deficiency in the period has a tracker entry showing progress through completion with timestamps; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of remediation tracking, or deficiencies left open without a documented timeline, is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A 3-person company's only deficiency during the period (a misconfigured storage bucket permission) was fixed the same day; the only record is a Slack thread with a before screenshot, the fix, and an after screenshot confirming closure, timestamped throughout.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Solo/small-team proportionality: a small company's real, timestamped Slack thread showing the deficiency identified and tracked through to a confirmed fix is a proportional substitute for a formal ticketing tool. Pass explicitly on this proportional basis.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual deficiency tracker showing progress and closure records (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that remediation is tracked to completion?

attributes.text: Capacity metrics are monitored for production systems
attributes.typical_evidence: Monitoring platform showing capacity metrics collected for production infrastructure
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Monitoring platform shows capacity metrics being collected for production systems, at minimum CPU/compute and storage utilization. FAIL: No capacity metrics monitored for production systems.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Availability TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The entity runs on managed Supabase Postgres and Vercel with no custom CloudWatch-style alarms configured, but the Supabase project dashboard natively displays CPU, connection, and storage utilization by default.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Compensating controls are a legitimate pass path: a managed platform's built-in capacity dashboard satisfies 'capacity metrics are monitored' even without the entity configuring its own alarms, since the metrics are actually being collected and visible.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A generic architecture diagram labeled 'monitoring in place' was submitted as evidence that CPU and storage utilization are tracked, with no actual dashboard, export, or config shown.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A diagram asserting a practice is not system proof of it. The attribute requires an actual monitoring platform view or export showing metrics being collected, not a claim illustrated in a diagram.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that capacity metrics are monitored for production systems?

attributes.text: Threshold-based alerts notify responsible personnel before capacity is exhausted
attributes.typical_evidence: Alert rule configuration showing capacity thresholds and notification targets
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Alert rule configuration shows threshold-based capacity alerts with defined trigger values and notification targets (email, chat, or paging). FAIL: No capacity threshold alerts configured for production systems.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Availability TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Capacity alerts are configured to post to a shared on-call Slack channel monitored on a rotation, rather than paging one named individual.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline: the pass criteria accept any defined notification target including chat, and do not require a specific named recipient. A monitored shared channel satisfies the notification requirement.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: CloudWatch alarms for capacity thresholds exist and were credited as configured, but the alarm state shown is 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA' because the alarms are not actually receiving live metric data.
calibration_examples.reasoning: An alarm that exists on paper but is not receiving live data is not functioning alerting. The evidence must show the alarm is actively evaluating real metrics, not merely defined.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that threshold-based alerts notify responsible personnel before capacity is exhausted?

attributes.text: Capacity is scaled or expanded when usage approaches tolerances
attributes.typical_evidence: Auto-scaling configuration, or documented capacity expansion procedure with trigger criteria
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Auto-scaling configuration is active for production systems, OR a documented capacity expansion procedure describes trigger criteria and expansion steps. FAIL: No auto-scaling and no documented capacity expansion procedure. FLAG: Manual expansion procedure exists but has never been exercised, flag for CPA review.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Availability TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A documented manual capacity expansion procedure defines clear trigger thresholds and expansion steps, but the entity has never had to invoke it since no capacity threshold has been approached.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The pass criteria explicitly treat a documented but never-exercised manual procedure as a flagged pass for CPA review, not an outright fail. A defined procedure with real trigger criteria satisfies the design-stage requirement even absent invocation.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Auto-scaling is enabled only on the web application tier; the production database, which also serves customer traffic, has no scaling or expansion configuration and no documented expansion procedure at all.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline requires coverage of production systems generally, not just the tier that happens to have scaling enabled. Partial coverage that excludes a production data store with neither auto-scaling nor a documented procedure is a systematic gap, not a pass.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that capacity is scaled or expanded when usage approaches tolerances?

attributes.text: Capacity is evaluated against current and forecasted demand at least annually
attributes.typical_evidence: Capacity review record or planning document comparing current usage to forecasted demand
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Capacity review record dated within the last 12 months compares current usage against forecasted demand and documents conclusions. Entity < 12 months old: pass if capacity review was performed during entity lifetime. FAIL: No documented capacity review within the last 12 months.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Availability TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Eight months ago the founder posted a Slack message comparing current usage against projected growth and concluding current capacity was adequate; no formal capacity planning report was produced.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes pass on the substance of the review being performed, not the formality of its write-up. The Slack message documents an actual comparison of current versus forecasted demand within the required window.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that capacity is evaluated against current?
Does the evidence show that forecasted demand at least annually?

attributes.text: Functional requirements (what the system does) and nonfunctional requirements (performance, availability, accuracy) are documented
attributes.typical_evidence: Product specification, API documentation, or system requirements document covering what the system processes and expected behavior
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes functional requirements (what the system processes and produces) and nonfunctional requirements (performance targets, accuracy expectations, availability SLAs). FAIL: No documented requirements for system processing.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Processing Integrity TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A live product spec doc in the company's engineering wiki describes exactly what each API endpoint processes, expected latency targets, and uptime commitments, but never uses the literal phrase 'functional requirements' or 'nonfunctional requirements'.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Judge what the evidence shows, not whether it uses the exact vocabulary of the attribute text. The spec document substantively covers what the system processes (functional) and performance/availability targets (nonfunctional), which is all the criteria requires.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A 40-page product requirements document describes dispatch matching, courier assignment, and order state transitions in detail. It contains no performance targets, no accuracy expectations for the matching logic, and no availability commitment. The client noted those live 'in the SLA we give enterprise customers', but no such document was provided.
calibration_examples.reasoning: This attribute names two categories of requirement and both have to be documented, so a strong functional specification with nothing nonfunctional in it is half the evidence. A reference to targets living in an unproduced customer contract does not document them for the entity's own processing.

attributes.text: For each processing error (if any): errors are corrected within the entity's defined SLA
attributes.typical_evidence: Error correction records showing detection timestamp, correction timestamp, and resolution details
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity corrects processing errors within a defined SLA (default: critical within 24 hours, non-critical within 5 business days), and either complete dated processing error history through the test date proves that no processing errors occurred, or the most recent error has a correction record with timestamps showing correction within the defined SLA. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the correction process and defined SLA remains required. FAIL if processing errors can occur with no correction process or defined SLA in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no processing errors occurred in the period, complete dated processing error history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If errors occurred, PASS if every processing error in the period was corrected within the defined SLA (default: critical within 24 hours, non-critical within 5 business days); isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic failure to correct errors within the SLA is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: No processing errors occurred at the company during the review period, and there is no error-correction record to test because there was nothing to correct.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists population attributes pass on the existence and use of the correction process, and this one explicitly passes by default when no errors occurred during the period. Marking a gap for an empty population ignores the pass criteria's own default-pass clause.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual error correction records showing detection timestamp (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that errors are corrected within the entity's defined sla?
