attributes.text: Privacy notice is published and accessible to data subjects before or at the time of data collection
attributes.typical_evidence: Published privacy notice URL, or documented delivery channel showing how data subjects receive the notice
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Privacy notice is published at a publicly accessible URL or provided to data subjects through a documented channel before or at the time of collection. FAIL: No privacy notice, or notice is not accessible to data subjects before collection.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A screenshot of the account sign-up flow shows a linked privacy notice presented to the user before they submit any personal information, but there is no separately hosted, publicly indexed privacy page.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Judge what the evidence shows: a documented delivery channel at the point of collection satisfies the criteria just as well as a standalone public URL. The sign-up flow screenshot demonstrates the notice was accessible before or at the time of collection, which is exactly what is required.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that privacy notice is published?
Does the evidence show that accessible to data subjects before or at the time of data collection?

attributes.text: Notice covers all required elements: types of personal information collected, purposes of use, third-party disclosures, data subject rights, and entities/activities covered
attributes.typical_evidence: Privacy notice document reviewed for completeness of required elements
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Privacy notice contains all 5 required elements: (1) types of personal information collected, (2) purposes of use, (3) third-party disclosures, (4) data subject rights, (5) description of entities and activities covered. FAIL: Privacy notice is missing any of the 5 required elements.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The published privacy notice has a section titled 'Who We Share Data With' listing categories of vendors and partners receiving data, covering the third-party disclosure requirement without using that phrase verbatim.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: the criteria checks for the substantive presence of each required element, not a section titled with the exact regulatory phrase. A section describing who data is shared with satisfies the third-party disclosure requirement.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The published privacy notice covers the categories of personal information collected, why each is used, the named third parties it is shared with, and how learners exercise access and deletion rights. It never describes which entities or activities it covers; the company operates the tutoring marketplace and a separate assessment product under different brands.
calibration_examples.reasoning: All five elements are required and the description of covered entities and activities is the one most often absent, so a notice that reads as thorough can still fail on scope. Where an entity runs more than one product, a notice that never says which entities and activities it governs leaves a data subject unable to tell whether it applies to them.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that notice covers all required elements: types of personal information collected, purposes of use, third-party disclosures, data subject rights?
Does the evidence show that entities/activities covered?

attributes.text: Notice is written in clear language and is current (dated within 24 months)
attributes.typical_evidence: Privacy notice showing date, plain-language structure, and headings
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Privacy notice uses plain language with headings, is dated or has a version date within the last 24 months, and is easily locatable (linked from footer, account settings, or sign-up flow). FAIL: Notice is undated, dated more than 24 months ago, or written entirely in legal jargon without plain-language summaries. FLAG: Notice uses technical terms without definitions, flag for CPA review.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The privacy notice was last substantively updated 10 months ago according to the internal version-history log in the CMS, but the public-facing page itself does not display a visible 'last updated' date to a casual reader.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Verify the corpus before failing: the underlying version-history record establishes the notice is current within 24 months, which is what the criteria actually tests, even though that date is not surfaced as a footer timestamp on the page itself.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that notice is written in clear language?
Does the evidence show that is current (dated within 24 months)?

attributes.text: Data subjects are informed when the notice changes, and prior versions are retained
attributes.typical_evidence: Version history or archive of prior privacy notices, and evidence of change notification (email, banner, or changelog)
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Prior versions of the privacy notice are retained (version history, archive, or web archive), AND a process exists for notifying data subjects of changes (email, banner, or documented procedure). FAIL: No prior versions retained, or no process for notifying data subjects of changes.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The privacy notice lives in the company's website content repository, where every prior version is preserved in commit history along with the date each change was published, and change announcements go out via an in-app banner; there is no formal public web-archive tool in use.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Solo/small-team proportionality: judge against a realistic minimum design rather than requiring a dedicated archiving product. A repository's version history preserving every prior notice, paired with a real in-app notification mechanism for changes, is a proportional and verifiable way to meet this requirement.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that data subjects are informed when the notice changes?
Does the evidence show that prior versions are retained?

attributes.text: Data subjects are informed of their choices and the consequences of denying consent
attributes.typical_evidence: Privacy notice or consent interface showing choices available and consequences of denying consent (e.g., service limitations)
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Privacy notice or consent interface informs data subjects of their choices regarding data collection/use and the consequences of denying consent (e.g., service limitations, reduced functionality). FAIL: No communication of choices or consequences of denying consent to data subjects.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The consent screen at sign-up includes one sentence noting that declining the optional data-sharing toggle will disable certain personalization features, rather than a dedicated 'consequences of denying consent' section.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: the criteria requires that consequences of denying consent be communicated, not that they occupy a labeled section of their own. A brief but clear statement of what happens if consent is declined satisfies the substance of the requirement.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that data subjects are informed of their choices?
Does the evidence show that the consequences of denying consent?

attributes.text: Consent is obtained before or at the time of collection through documented mechanisms
attributes.typical_evidence: Consent mechanism in the product (sign-up flow checkbox, cookie banner, or opt-in form) with consent record storage
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: System configuration shows consent mechanisms implemented at collection points (sign-up flow, cookie consent, opt-in forms) and consent records stored with timestamp and data subject identifier. FAIL: No consent mechanisms at collection points, or consent records are not maintained.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A screenshot of the cookie-consent banner is paired with a database table screenshot showing consent records stored with timestamp and user identifier for each acceptance, but there is no separate written consent-management policy document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline: this is a config attribute, so the consent-capture mechanism and its stored records are the correct and sufficient evidence, not a placeholder awaiting a written policy. The configuration demonstrates consent is obtained and recorded exactly as the criteria requires.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The client submitted a spreadsheet they manually typed logging 'consents received' by date and user name, with no export or screenshot from the actual consent-capture system or database.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A client-authored spreadsheet is not system proof; a consent-record claim for a config attribute needs a capture of the system that actually stores consent. A hand-typed log does not establish that consent is genuinely captured and retained by the system.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that consent is obtained before or at the time of collection through documented mechanisms?

attributes.text: Explicit consent is obtained separately for sensitive information and cross-border data transfers
attributes.typical_evidence: Separate consent mechanism for sensitive data (health, financial, biometric) and cross-border transfers, not bundled with general consent
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: If sensitive information or cross-border transfers occur, separate explicit consent mechanism exists (not bundled with general consent). If no sensitive data collected and no cross-border transfers, pass by default. FAIL: Sensitive information collected or cross-border transfers occur without separate explicit consent.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if no sensitive personal information collected and no cross-border data transfers

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The signup flow screenshot shows an unbundled, separately checked consent for the health and dietary information collected about children in care. The vendor register shows the support desk tool processes ticket contents, including that information, in another region; consent for that transfer is covered only by acceptance of the general terms at signup.
calibration_examples.reasoning: This attribute has two triggers and separate explicit consent is required for each one that is present, so satisfying it for sensitive information does not satisfy it for cross-border transfer. Bundling the transfer into general terms acceptance is exactly the bundling the criteria exclude.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that explicit consent is obtained separately for sensitive information?
Does the system configuration show that cross-border data transfers?

attributes.text: New consent is obtained before using data for purposes not previously disclosed
attributes.typical_evidence: Procedure for obtaining consent for new data uses, or evidence of re-consent notifications sent when purposes change
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for obtaining new consent before using personal information for purposes not in the original privacy notice, OR complete dated personal-information use history proves no new purposes were introduced during the period (record non-occurrence for this alternative). FAIL: Personal information used for new purposes without obtaining new consent.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company did not introduce any new uses for previously collected personal information during the review period, and there is no re-consent notification or new-purposes procedure document to point to.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes with an explicit pass-by-default clause pass when the triggering event never occurred. The pass criteria for this attribute states that no new purposes introduced during the period is a pass by default, so the absence of a re-consent process document is not itself a gap.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that new consent is obtained before using data for purposes not previously disclosed?

attributes.text: Personal information collected matches what is described in the privacy notice, no undisclosed collection
attributes.typical_evidence: Comparison of data fields collected by the system (database schema, form fields, API inputs) against the privacy notice's description of collected data
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Comparison of actual data collection fields against the privacy notice shows no personal information collected beyond what is described. FAIL: System collects personal information not described in the privacy notice.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A comparison of the production database schema against the privacy notice shows a hashed device identifier field used only for fraud prevention, which the AI flagged as undisclosed collection, though the notice's general 'device and usage information' clause covers it.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: a general category disclosure in the privacy notice can cover a specific field without listing every field name individually. The hashed device identifier falls within the disclosed 'device and usage information' category, so this is not undisclosed collection.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The evidence submitted for this attribute is a screenshot of a third-party analytics vendor's public page describing their own data-minimization practices, offered as proof of what personal information this org collects.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A provider's marketing or trust page is not this organization's own configuration. The criteria requires a comparison of this entity's actual collected data fields against its own privacy notice, not a vendor's unrelated public claims.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that personal information collected matches what is described in the privacy notice — no undisclosed collection?

attributes.text: Collection methods are documented and comply with applicable legal requirements
attributes.typical_evidence: Data collection inventory or data flow document listing collection methods, sources, and legal basis for each data category
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document lists data collection methods and sources with legal basis identified for each category of personal information collected. FAIL: Collection methods or sources are not documented, or no legal basis identified.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A data-flow document in the company wiki lists each category of personal information, its collection method, and its source, with the legal-basis column filled in tersely as 'legitimate interest' or 'consent' for every row rather than a detailed legal analysis.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes pass on the existence and identification of the required content, not on the depth or polish of its write-up. A terse but present legal-basis designation for each category satisfies the criteria, which only asks that a legal basis be identified.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The data map documents eleven collection points captured directly from users, each with its method and a stated legal basis. It is silent on the two data enrichment vendors from which the company buys additional business contact records, which the vendor register and two invoices confirm are in use.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A collection inventory has to cover every source personal information arrives from, not only the ones where the data subject is present. Acquired records are the collection method most often left out of a data map and the most likely to lack a legal basis, so omitting that source entirely is a gap rather than an incomplete detail.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that collection methods are documented?
Does the evidence show that comply with applicable legal requirements?

attributes.text: Data subjects are informed when additional personal information is acquired beyond original collection
attributes.typical_evidence: Notification procedure or evidence of notifications sent when additional data was acquired from third-party sources
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Documented procedure exists for notifying data subjects when additional personal information is acquired beyond the original collection scope, OR complete dated acquisition history proves no additional personal information was acquired during the period (record non-occurrence for this alternative). FAIL: Additional personal information acquired without notifying data subjects.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company did not acquire any additional personal information beyond its original collection scope during the review period, and there is no notification record or procedure document specific to that scenario.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes with an explicit pass-by-default clause pass when the triggering event never occurred. The pass criteria for this attribute states that no additional information acquired during the period is a pass by default, so the absence of a notification record is not itself a gap.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that data subjects are informed when additional personal information is acquired beyond original collection?

attributes.text: For all information retained beyond its original purpose (if any): explicit consent to retain is documented
attributes.typical_evidence: Consent records showing explicit consent for retention of personal information beyond the original collection purpose
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity documents explicit consent when information is retained beyond its original purpose, and either complete dated retention and purpose history through the test date proves that no information is retained beyond its original purpose, or the most recent instance has documented explicit consent for retention with timestamp and data subject identifier. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the explicit consent process remains required. FAIL if information can be retained beyond its original purpose with no explicit consent process in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no information was retained beyond its original purpose in the period, complete dated retention and purpose history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If retention beyond purpose occurred, PASS if every instance in the period has documented explicit consent for retention with timestamp and data subject identifier; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic retention beyond purpose without documented consent is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: No personal information was retained beyond its original collection purpose during the review period, so there is no consent-to-retain record to test.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists population attributes pass on the existence and use of the consent-to-retain process, and this one explicitly passes by default when no such retention occurred during the period. Requiring a consent record to exist when the underlying trigger never happened ignores the pass criteria's own default-pass clause.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual consent records showing explicit consent for retention of personal information beyond the original collection purpose (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that explicit consent to retain is documented?

attributes.text: Policy or controls restrict use of personal information to disclosed purposes
attributes.typical_evidence: Data use policy or privacy policy section describing purpose limitation, or system configuration showing access restrictions by purpose
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Policy document or system configuration shows controls restricting use of personal information to purposes disclosed in the privacy notice (purpose-limitation policy, access restrictions by purpose, or documented use guidelines). FAIL: No policy or controls limiting personal information use to disclosed purposes.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company's privacy policy has a 'How We Use Your Information' section listing each disclosed purpose, and the product's admin console restricts analytics/marketing feature access by role so engineers can't repurpose data outside those listed uses.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A pass-criteria clause is satisfied by substance, not by matching a specific document title. The pass criteria names 'access restrictions by purpose' as an accepted form, so the policy section plus the role-gated feature access together constitute a real purpose-limitation control even without a document literally titled 'Purpose Limitation Policy.'

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that policy or controls restrict use of personal information to disclosed purposes?

attributes.text: Actual uses of personal information align with the privacy notice, no undisclosed uses
attributes.typical_evidence: Data processing inventory or system audit showing how personal information is used, compared against purposes in the privacy notice
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Comparison of actual personal information uses (features, analytics, marketing, sharing) against the privacy notice shows all uses are disclosed. FAIL: Personal information is used for purposes not disclosed in the privacy notice without separate consent.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A live screenshot of the analytics platform's data-category settings shows only the categories listed in the privacy notice (product usage, billing) are enabled; no marketing or resale categories are toggled on.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Live system screenshots are system evidence regardless of how they were labeled at submission, this was filed generically as 'screenshot' rather than a formal data-processing inventory, but it plainly shows actual uses matching disclosed purposes. Judge what the evidence shows, not its filename.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The founder typed up a spreadsheet titled 'Our data uses' listing the same purposes as the privacy notice, with no export or screenshot from any actual system pulling this from configuration.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A client-authored spreadsheet is not system proof for a config attribute, it asserts alignment rather than demonstrating it. Actual-use claims need provenance (a system export/screenshot) or corroboration against a live system view, not a hand-typed restatement of the policy.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that actual uses of personal information align with the privacy notice — no undisclosed uses?

attributes.text: Documented process exists for receiving and responding to data subject access and correction requests
attributes.typical_evidence: Data subject rights procedure describing how access/correction requests are received, verified, fulfilled, and tracked, with defined response timeframes
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for receiving, verifying identity, fulfilling, and responding to data subject access and correction requests, with defined response timeframe (default: 30 days). FAIL: No documented process for data subject access or correction requests.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A support-team runbook article walks through how a data access request comes into the shared inbox, how the requester's identity is checked, how the export is generated, and a 30-day SLA badge on the ticket queue, but the article is titled 'Handling Data Requests,' not 'Data Subject Rights Policy.'
calibration_examples.reasoning: Process-exists attributes pass on the existence and use of the process, not on matching a specific document title. The runbook covers intake, verification, fulfillment, and timeframe, everything the attribute asks for, so it passes despite the informal name.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a documented process for data subject requests?
Does the process cover receiving and responding to access requests?
Does the process cover receiving and responding to correction requests?

attributes.text: Data subjects' identity is verified before providing access to their personal information
attributes.typical_evidence: Identity verification procedure or evidence of verification steps (email confirmation, account authentication, ID verification)
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes identity verification steps performed before providing access to personal information (email confirmation, account authentication, or ID verification). FAIL: No identity verification procedures for access requests.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Access requests are only fulfilled after the requester logs into their existing authenticated account session; there is no separate ID-check or email-confirmation step beyond the standard login.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Never import a stricter requirement than the attribute text specifies, the pass criteria names account authentication explicitly alongside email confirmation and ID verification. Existing account authentication is a legitimate identity-verification method, so requiring a redundant separate step over-reads the attribute.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that data subjects' identity is verified before providing access to their personal information?

attributes.text: Data subjects can update or correct their personal information through self-service or request
attributes.typical_evidence: Self-service profile settings or documented correction request process showing how data subjects can update their information
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: System provides self-service update capability (account settings, profile page) or a documented request-based correction process. Corrections are propagated to third parties previously provided the data. FAIL: No mechanism for data subjects to update or correct their personal information.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A screenshot of the account settings page shows editable name, email, and preference fields the user can change directly and save, filed under a generic 'UI screenshots' evidence batch rather than a dedicated privacy-rights folder.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A live capture plainly showing self-service update capability passes even when it wasn't itemized or filed under a privacy-specific label. The screenshot demonstrates the exact mechanism the attribute asks for.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company's public marketing site states 'You can update your information anytime in your dashboard,' but no screenshot or export of the actual settings page was provided.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A provider's marketing or public-facing page is not proof of the product's actual configuration. The attribute requires evidence the self-service mechanism exists in the live system, not a promise made on a marketing page.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that data subjects can update or correct their personal information through self-service or request?

attributes.text: Denials of access or correction requests include written reasons and appeal information
attributes.typical_evidence: Denial response template or procedure including reason for denial and appeal instructions
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: for every access or correction request DENIED in the period, the response to the data subject gives written reasons and tells them how to appeal. FAIL: a request was denied and the response gave no reason, or no appeal route. If the population was empty for the period, this is not a pass by default: show the place these are recorded, empty, over the period, and record it as non-occurrence. Where no request has ever been denied, a template showing the reasons-and-appeal wording is not a pass here; it is good practice and it belongs to A1, which tests the documented process.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A two-person startup has never received or denied a data access or correction request, and has no denial-letter template on file.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Apply the criteria's own default-pass clause before flagging an absence as a gap, the pass criteria explicitly states this attribute passes by default when no denials have occurred. A naive read fails it for lacking an artifact the criteria says isn't required in this scenario.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The client stated no access or correction requests were denied, so no denial letters were provided. The request log they supplied shows two requests closed with the status 'rejected, could not verify', and the outbound messages for both read in full 'We are unable to process this request at this time.'
calibration_examples.reasoning: A pass by default for a non-occurrence fails the moment the entity's own log shows the event occurred, whatever the client believes happened. Two requests were denied, and the messages sent carry neither a written reason nor any appeal instruction, which is precisely what this attribute requires a denial to include.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that denials of access or correction requests include written reasons?
Does the evidence show that appeal information?

attributes.text: For each access/correction request (if any): requests are responded to within the defined timeframe
attributes.typical_evidence: Request tracking records showing receipt date, response date, and resolution for each access/correction request
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity responds to access and correction requests within a defined timeframe (default: 30 days), and either complete dated access and correction request history through the test date proves that no requests were received, or the most recent request was responded to within the defined timeframe with personal information provided in an understandable format. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the response process and defined timeframe remains required. FAIL if access and correction requests can be received with no defined response process or timeframe in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no access or correction requests were received in the period, complete dated access and correction request history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If requests were received, PASS if every request in the period was responded to within the defined timeframe (default: 30 days) with personal information provided in an understandable format; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic failure to respond within the timeframe is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The data-subject-rights runbook defines a 30-day response window and a named owner, and the company has never received an access or correction request in its operating history, so there are no fulfilled tickets to test.
calibration_examples.reasoning: At the design/Type I stage this attribute passes when a defined response timeframe is in place and no requests have been received, the criteria states this default explicitly. The population is empty because the triggering event never occurred, so treating the empty population as a gap misapplies the criteria.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual request tracking records showing receipt date (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that requests are responded to within the defined timeframe?

attributes.text: Personal information is disclosed only for approved purposes to third parties with privacy agreements
attributes.typical_evidence: Policy restricting disclosures to approved purposes and authorized recipients, with evidence that privacy policies are communicated to third parties before disclosure
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Policy restricts personal information disclosure to approved purposes and authorized third parties as described in the privacy notice, and privacy requirements are communicated to third parties before disclosure. FAIL: No controls limiting disclosures to approved purposes and authorized recipients.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Vendor data-processing agreements contain confidentiality and purpose-limitation clauses restricting each subprocessor to the specific services they were engaged for, but there is no standalone 'third-party disclosure policy' document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Never import a stricter requirement than the attribute text specifies, the pass criteria asks for controls restricting disclosure to approved purposes and privacy requirements communicated to third parties, and contractual purpose-limitation clauses satisfy exactly that. A standalone policy document is one way to satisfy it, not the only way.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The privacy policy restricts disclosure to approved purposes, and signed data processing agreements are on file for the three largest processors. Two further vendors that receive couple and guest contact details, an email delivery service and a post-event survey tool, have no privacy terms on file; both were onboarded directly by the marketing lead.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The requirement to communicate privacy requirements before disclosure applies to every third party that receives personal information, not to the ones large enough to have gone through procurement. Agreements covering the major processors leave the smaller recipients unbound, and those are usually the ones acquired outside any review.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that personal information is disclosed only for approved purposes to third parties with privacy agreements?

attributes.text: Records of authorized disclosures are maintained (who, what, when, to whom)
attributes.typical_evidence: Disclosure log or data sharing records showing authorized disclosures with recipient, data type, date, and purpose
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: System maintains records of authorized disclosures including recipient, data type, date, and purpose. FAIL: No authorized disclosure records maintained.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: An export from the company's integration platform lists each outbound data-sharing event with destination, data fields, and timestamp, submitted as a raw CSV export rather than a formatted 'disclosure register.'
calibration_examples.reasoning: A system export is system evidence regardless of its formatting or filename, it shows recipient, data type, date, and purpose exactly as required. Don't fail evidence for lacking a polished presentation when the substance is a genuine system-generated record.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A spreadsheet titled 'Vendor disclosures 2026' was typed up by the ops lead from memory, listing vendor names and rough dates, with no underlying system log or export to corroborate the entries.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A client-authored spreadsheet reconstructed from memory is not reliable disclosure proof, records need to be system-maintained or corroborated against an actual system view, with the recipient/data/date/purpose fields the criteria requires. Recall-based entries missing timestamps and a source system carry no evidentiary weight.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that records of authorized disclosures are maintained (who, what, when, to whom)?

attributes.text: Records of unauthorized disclosures (breaches) are maintained
attributes.typical_evidence: Breach register or incident log tracking unauthorized disclosures with detection date, scope, and response actions
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: System maintains a breach register or incident log for unauthorized disclosures. If no unauthorized disclosures occurred, register exists and is empty (pass). FAIL: No mechanism for recording unauthorized disclosures.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company's incident-tracking tool has a 'Privacy Breach' category that has never had an entry logged against it; the tracker itself was set up eight months ago and shows zero incidents.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Config attributes for a register pass on the mechanism existing, not on it having contents, the pass criteria explicitly treats an empty register as a pass when no breaches occurred. Flagging an empty-but-functional register as a gap misapplies the criteria's own default.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: In an interview, the head of engineering said 'we'd log any breach in our internal tracker if one happened,' but no screenshot, export, or actual tracker view was provided.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Verbal confirmation is never config evidence, a described capability with no system capture to back it up doesn't demonstrate the mechanism actually exists. The attribute needs a record or screenshot of the tracker itself, not an assurance about it.

coverage_checks.question: Does the system configuration show that records of unauthorized disclosures (breaches) are maintained?

attributes.text: Process exists to remediate misuse of personal information by third parties

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The standard vendor MSA includes a clause requiring immediate remediation, corrective action, and a right to terminate on discovery of unauthorized data use, but there is no separate 'third-party misuse remediation procedure' document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Never fail an attribute for lacking a specific artifact form when the criteria's own substance is met by another form, the criteria asks for remediation steps (investigation, contract enforcement, relationship termination), and the MSA clause describes exactly those. A standalone procedure document is not required.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a third-party misuse remediation procedure or contractual terms addressing remediation of unauthorized use?

attributes.text: For each third party receiving personal information: privacy compliance is assessed and breach reporting commitments are on file
attributes.typical_evidence: Third-party privacy assessment records and contractual breach notification clauses for each recipient of personal information
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity assesses privacy compliance of third parties receiving personal information and obtains breach reporting commitments, and either complete dated third-party disclosure history through the test date proves that no third-party disclosures occurred, or the most recent third party has a privacy compliance assessment on file and a contractual commitment to report unauthorized disclosures. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the privacy assessment and breach reporting commitment process remains required. TYPE II (over the period): If no third-party disclosures occurred in the period, complete dated third-party disclosure history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A solo-founder company has two subprocessors (a cloud host and an email provider); the founder documented, in a short vendor-review note, that both publish current SOC 2 reports and that their standard DPAs include breach-notification clauses, but no formal privacy-assessment questionnaire was completed.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Compensating controls are a legitimate pass path at design stage, for a solo founder, a documented review of a vendor's public security attestation plus the DPA's breach clause stands in for a formal assessment questionnaire. The basis is real, verifiable, and documented, so it passes on a proportional basis.

calibration_examples.reasoning: Identification of breach-reporting requirements passes on substance regardless of the document's title or location. The runbook table actually names the regulatory timelines, recipients, and contractual obligations the criteria asks for, so failing it for not being a standalone titled document imports a form requirement the attribute doesn't state.

attributes.text: Breach notification procedures define timelines, responsible parties, and notification content
attributes.typical_evidence: Breach notification procedure with defined timelines, responsible parties, and notification templates or content requirements
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Procedure defines notification timelines meeting regulatory requirements, identifies responsible parties for executing notifications, and describes required notification content. FAIL: No breach notification procedures, or procedures lack timelines, responsible parties, or content requirements.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The breach notification timeline, responsible-party assignment, and required notification content are all defined within a section of the company's broader incident response plan rather than in a standalone breach-notification document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Never import a requirement the attribute text doesn't state, nothing in the criteria requires a standalone document, only that timelines, responsible parties, and content are defined somewhere. A well-integrated section of the incident response plan satisfies the same substance.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The incident response plan's breach section reads in full: 'In the event of a breach of personal information, the company will notify affected individuals and applicable regulators as required by law.' No timeline, no named role, and no description of what a notification must contain appears anywhere in the plan or its appendices.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A commitment to comply is not a procedure, and this attribute requires timelines, responsible parties, and notification content, none of which a sentence restating the legal obligation supplies. A plan that would leave the responder looking up all three during the incident has not defined the procedure.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that breach notification procedures define timelines, responsible parties?

attributes.text: For each breach (if any): notifications were sent within required timelines
attributes.typical_evidence: Breach notification records showing notification date, recipients, and content for each breach
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity notifies affected parties and regulators of breaches within required timelines, and either complete dated breach history through the test date proves that no breaches occurred, or the most recent breach has notification records showing affected parties and regulators notified within required timelines. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the breach notification process and required timelines remains required. FAIL if breaches can occur with no breach notification process in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no breaches occurred in the period, complete dated breach history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If breaches occurred, PASS if every breach in the period has notification records showing affected parties and regulators notified within required timelines; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic failure to notify within required timelines is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company has never experienced a data breach in its operating history, and has no breach notification records to test.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The pass criteria explicitly defaults to pass when no breaches occurred during the period, the population is empty because the triggering event never happened. Apply the criteria's own default rather than treating absence of breach records as a gap.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual breach notification records showing notification date (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that notifications were sent within required timelines?

attributes.text: Personal information types and handling processes are documented
attributes.typical_evidence: Data inventory or records of processing activities (ROPA) listing personal information types, handling processes, and third parties involved
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document lists types of personal information held, handling processes for each type, and third parties involved in processing. FAIL: No documented inventory of personal information types or handling processes.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A Notion database lists every category of personal information collected, which system stores it, and which third parties process it, functioning as the company's data map, but it isn't formatted as a formal 'Records of Processing Activities' document.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism, the attribute asks for personal information types, handling processes, and third parties involved to be documented, and a maintained Notion data map does exactly that. The specific artifact name (ROPA) is typical evidence, not a required label.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that personal information types?

attributes.text: Process exists for responding to accounting requests about personal information held and disclosed
attributes.typical_evidence: Procedure for responding to data controller or data subject requests for an accounting of personal information
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for responding to requests for an accounting of personal information held and disclosed, including how requests are captured and communicated. FAIL: No documented process for accounting requests.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company's single combined data-subject-rights procedure covers access, correction, and 'tell me what you have on me' accounting requests in one document rather than as a separate accounting-request procedure.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline cuts both ways, the attribute needs the described accounting-request process to exist, not to exist as its own standalone document. A combined procedure that genuinely covers accounting requests satisfies this attribute even though it's bundled with the access/correction process.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The privacy notice instructs users to email a privacy address at the company domain to request an accounting of the personal information held about them. The mail administrator's screenshot shows that address is a distribution list with no members, and the client confirmed nothing forwards from it and no queue or ticket type exists for these requests.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A documented channel satisfies this attribute only if requests arriving on it are actually captured, because the criterion asks how requests are captured and communicated, not merely how they are invited. An address that routes to nobody is a published intake with no process behind it.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a procedure for responding to data controller or data subject requests for an accounting of personal information?

attributes.text: For each accounting request (if any): requests are responded to within defined timeframes
attributes.typical_evidence: Request tracking records showing receipt date, response date, and information provided for each accounting request
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if the entity responds to accounting requests within defined timeframes, and either complete dated accounting request history through the test date proves that no accounting requests were received, or the most recent request was responded to within the defined timeframe with documentation of personal information held and disclosures made. For the proved-empty alternative, record non-occurrence; the response process and defined timeframe remains required. FAIL if accounting requests can be received with no defined response process or timeframe in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no accounting requests were received in the period, complete dated accounting request history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If requests were received, PASS if every accounting request in the period was responded to within the defined timeframe with documentation of personal information held and disclosures made; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic failure to respond within the timeframe is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company has never received a request for an accounting of personal information held and disclosed.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The pass criteria defaults to pass when no accounting requests were received during the period. The population is empty when the underlying event never occurred, so this isn't a gap.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual request tracking records showing receipt date (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show that requests are responded to within defined timeframes?

attributes.text: Processes maintain personal information accuracy and completeness (validation at collection and self-service updates)
attributes.typical_evidence: Data quality controls documentation showing validation at collection, self-service update capability, or periodic data quality checks
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes processes for maintaining personal information accuracy and completeness, at minimum data validation at collection points and a mechanism for data subjects to update their information (self-service or request-based). FAIL: No processes for maintaining personal information accuracy and completeness.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The signup form enforces required-field and email-format validation at collection, and the account settings page lets users edit their own profile data afterward; both are described briefly in the engineering wiki rather than a standalone 'Data Quality Policy.'
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism, the pass criteria asks for validation at collection plus a self-service update mechanism, both of which are present and documented, just not under a dedicated policy title. Judge the substance of the controls, not the label of the document describing them.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The data handling document describes validation at collection in detail: email verification, phone format checks, and duplicate detection on employer records. On updates it says only that 'candidates may contact us to correct their information.' There is no self-service edit path in the product and no written intake, owner, or timeframe for those contacts.
calibration_examples.reasoning: This attribute sets a floor of two things, validation at collection and a mechanism for data subjects to update their information, so meeting one of them well does not carry the other. An invitation to get in touch, with nothing behind it describing how a correction is received and applied, is not a mechanism.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that processes maintain personal information accuracy?
Does the evidence show that completeness (validation at collection?
Does the evidence show that self-service updates)?

attributes.text: Personal information is reviewed periodically to ensure it remains relevant to identified purposes
attributes.typical_evidence: Data minimization review records, retention review, or data relevance assessment showing unnecessary data identified and removed
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a periodic review process for ensuring personal information remains relevant to identified purposes, including removal or archiving of unnecessary data. Entity < 12 months old: pass if review is scheduled. FAIL: No process for reviewing personal information relevance.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: An eight-month-old startup has a data-minimization review scheduled on its roadmap for next quarter but has not yet conducted one.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Solo/early-stage proportionality applies here explicitly in the criteria, entities under twelve months old pass if the review is scheduled, since a periodic review can't yet have a first cycle to point to. Judge against the minimum acceptable design for a young company, not a mature review history.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that personal information is reviewed periodically to ensure it remains relevant to identified purposes?

attributes.text: Contact information for privacy inquiries and complaints is published and accessible to data subjects
attributes.typical_evidence: Privacy notice or website showing published contact information (email, form, or phone) for privacy inquiries
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Privacy notice or website publishes contact information (email, form, or phone) for privacy inquiries and complaints, accessible to data subjects. FAIL: No published contact information for privacy inquiries.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The privacy policy footer lists a single support@company.com inbox for all inquiries, including privacy questions and complaints, rather than a dedicated privacy@ address.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Judge against the minimum acceptable design for a small company, the criteria accepts a published email, and a single monitored support inbox that genuinely handles privacy inquiries is a proportional substitute for a dedicated privacy mailbox. Structural absence of any contact channel would fail; a shared but functioning one passes.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence show that contact information for privacy inquiries?
Does the evidence show that complaints is published?
Does the evidence show that accessible to data subjects?

attributes.text: Documented process exists for receiving, investigating, and resolving privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes
attributes.typical_evidence: Privacy complaint handling procedure with intake, investigation, resolution, and communication steps including response timeframes
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Document describes a process for receiving, investigating, and resolving privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes, with defined response timeframes and resolution communication steps. FAIL: No documented process for handling privacy inquiries, complaints, or disputes.
attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The complaint-handling steps (intake via support ticket, escalation to the founder, target resolution window) are described as a section within the general privacy policy rather than in a standalone complaint-handling procedure.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism, the attribute requires the process to be documented and cover receiving, investigating, and resolving complaints, not that it live in its own document. A clearly described process embedded in a broader policy satisfies the same substance.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Submitted as the privacy complaint process: the customer support SLA, which defines a 24 hour first response, resolution targets by plan tier, and an escalation ladder to the support manager. Nothing in it mentions privacy, an investigation step, the privacy owner, or how a resolution is communicated to a data subject.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A general support SLA is not a privacy complaint procedure, and a documented timeframe for answering tickets does not establish the investigation and resolution steps this attribute names. Privacy disputes route differently, are owned by a different person, and end in a communicated determination rather than a closed ticket.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a documented process for privacy complaints?
Does the process cover receiving privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes?
Does the process cover investigating complaints?
Does the process cover resolving complaints and disputes?

attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

attributes.na_condition: N/A if Privacy TSC not in scope

FAIL if disputes can be received with no resolution and communication process in place. TYPE II (over the period): If no disputes were received in the period, complete dated dispute history covering the full period must prove the empty population; record non-occurrence. If disputes were received, PASS if every dispute in the period has a resolution record documenting the outcome and evidence of communication to the data subject; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of documented resolution or communication is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The company has never received a privacy complaint or dispute from a data subject, and so has no dispute resolution records on file.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The pass criteria defaults to pass when no disputes were received during the period, the population is empty because the triggering event never occurred. attributes.typical_evidence: Branch protection configuration for the production branch showing direct pushes and force pushes are not permitted
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Branch protection configuration for the production branch shows that direct pushes are not permitted and changes can only reach the branch through a merge. Force pushes are disabled. FAIL: The production branch allows direct pushes, has no branch protection, or permits force pushes.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A GitHub API export (raw JSON, not a console screenshot) of the production branch protection rule shows required_pull_request_reviews enabled and allow_force_pushes set to false.
calibration_examples.reasoning: No over-literalism: a live API export showing the substance of branch protection passes just as a console screenshot would. The format of the capture does not matter if it plainly shows direct and force pushes are blocked.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The engineering handbook states from memory that 'production branch is protected and can't be pushed to directly,' with no GitHub settings export or screenshot attached.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A client-authored description of a configuration is not system proof of that configuration. Branch protection is a config attribute that needs an actual GitHub settings export or screenshot, not a handbook claim.

coverage_checks.question: Does the branch protection configuration show that direct pushes to the production branch are blocked?
Does the configuration show that force pushes to the production branch are disabled?

attributes.text: Branch protection enforcement applies to administrators with no bypass
attributes.typical_evidence: Branch protection configuration showing administrator enforcement is enabled
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Branch protection configuration shows enforcement is applied to administrators, so no privileged account can bypass the required checks or the merge requirement. FAIL: Administrators can bypass branch protection, or the administrator enforcement setting is disabled.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A cropped GitHub branch protection screenshot shows the 'Include administrators' toggle in the on position, but the rest of the settings page is cut off from the capture.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A live capture plainly showing the substance passes even if it is not a full-page screenshot. The visible toggle is the exact setting the attribute tests, so a partial crop that still shows it is sufficient.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The founder verbally confirms in the review call that 'admin enforcement is always on for the production branch,' with no GitHub settings export submitted.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Verbal confirmation is never config evidence. The administrator-enforcement setting must be shown in an actual branch protection configuration export, not asserted in conversation.

attributes.text: Required status checks must pass before a change can merge to a production branch
attributes.typical_evidence: Branch protection required status checks configuration listing the checks that must pass, plus the CI workflow definition that produces them
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Branch protection configuration lists one or more required status checks that must report success before a merge is allowed, and the corresponding CI workflow exists and runs on changes to the production branch. FAIL: No status checks are required for merging, or required checks are configured but the referenced CI workflow does not exist or does not run.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Branch protection configuration for the production branch requires only a single 'build' status check to pass before merge, and the corresponding CI workflow runs on every pull request.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Attribute-boundary discipline: the pass criteria requires 'one or more' required status checks, not a specific number or a comprehensive test suite. A single enforced, functioning check satisfies the attribute as written.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A CI workflow file defining a test suite exists in the repository, but the branch protection settings export shows required_status_checks is null, meaning nothing is actually enforced at merge time.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The mere existence of a CI workflow is not the same as the workflow being required for merge. The system configuration must actually show the check listed as required, and here it does not.

coverage_checks.question: Does the configuration show that one or more status checks are required to pass before merging to production?
Does the evidence show the CI workflow that produces the required checks exists and runs on changes?

attributes.text: For each merged change: the change is traceable and carries a description and passing required checks
attributes.typical_evidence: Merged pull request or merge request records showing a description, the passing required status checks, and the commit history linking the change to the production branch
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if each inspected merged change has a description explaining the change, shows the required status checks passed before the merge, and is traceable to its commit history on the production branch. FAIL if any inspected change has no description, merged with failing or missing required checks, or cannot be traced to a merge. TYPE II (over the period): PASS if every merged change across the period carries a description and passing required checks; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of descriptions or of passing checks is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: For a solo-developer company, the merged pull requests show a description of the change and passing required CI checks, but were self-approved by the same developer who authored them, since no second engineer exists.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Never import a neighbor attribute's requirement: this attribute only requires a description, passing required checks, and traceability, not a second-person approval, which belongs to a separate peer-review control. Judged against its own text, the merges pass.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Each of the three inspected merged changes has a clear description and a green status check visible on the pull request. On one of them the merge commit is timestamped 14:02 and the required test run finished at 14:41, having been triggered on the main branch after the merge.
calibration_examples.reasoning: The checks have to pass before the merge, because a check that runs afterwards tells the entity what it shipped rather than gating whether it ships. A green badge read at fieldwork time hides the ordering, so the timestamps are the evidence, not the badge.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include an actual merged change record such as a pull request or merge request (not just a verbal description)?
Does the record show the merged change carries a description of what changed?
Does the record show the required status checks passed before the merge?

attributes.text: A post deployment verification practice confirms each deployed change works as intended
attributes.typical_evidence: Records of checks performed after deployment such as monitoring dashboards, health check results, smoke test output, or deployment logs showing verification after release
attributes.pass_criteria: DESIGN & TYPE I (as of a date): PASS if {company_name} performs a defined verification after each deployment such as automated health checks, smoke tests, or a monitoring review, and evidence shows this was done for a recent deployment. FAIL if there is no verification after deployment, or it is only described verbally with no supporting record. TYPE II (over the period): PASS if every deployment across the period shows verification was performed; isolated misses in an otherwise working practice are an exception, not a gap; systematic absence of verification after deployment is a gap.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The deployment platform's dashboard automatically runs a post-deploy health check and shows a green 'Deployment Ready' status with response-time metrics for the most recent release, captured as a screenshot.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A live capture plainly showing the substance passes even without a separately written 'verification log.' An automated platform health check tied to the deployment is exactly the kind of record the attribute asks for.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The deployment pipeline definition includes a smoke test stage with real assertions against the ticketing checkout path. The run log for the most recent production deployment shows that stage as 'skipped', because it is configured to run only when a manual flag is set, and no monitoring review or other verification was recorded for that deployment.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A verification practice has to have been performed for a recent deployment, so a configured stage that did not run is a defined intention rather than evidence. A conditional gate that defaults to skipped will be skipped exactly when it matters, which is why the attribute asks for the run and not the configuration.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a record of verification performed after a deployment such as health check results, smoke test output, or a monitoring review?
Does the record show the verification confirmed the deployed change was working as intended?

attributes.text: A current inventory of every device that accesses production is maintained
attributes.typical_evidence: Device inventory listing each production-accessing laptop and the person assigned to it, dated recently
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: An inventory lists every device used to access production, each tied to a named owner, and the device count is at least the number of people who access production. FAIL: No inventory exists, or a device known to access production is missing from it, or the inventory is undated and cannot be confirmed as current. NOTE: For a founder-managed environment the inventory may be a simple maintained list; what matters is that it is complete and current, not its format.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A two-founder company maintains a simple shared spreadsheet listing each founder's laptop, serial number, and owner, updated within the past week.
calibration_examples.reasoning: For a founder-managed environment the attribute's own note allows the inventory to be a simple maintained list. A current, complete spreadsheet tying each device to its owner passes on that proportional basis rather than being gapped for lacking a formal asset-management tool.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: The device inventory lists nine laptops, each tied to a named owner and updated last month. The identity provider shows twelve accounts with production access; three of those people appear nowhere in the device inventory, and two of them are contractors known to work from their own machines.
calibration_examples.reasoning: This attribute sets an explicit floor, that the device count is at least the number of people who access production, so a well maintained list that is short of that floor still fails. Devices missing from the inventory are usually personal or contractor machines, which are the ones no endpoint control reaches.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include a maintained list of devices that access production?
Does the inventory tie each device to a named owner and cover everyone who accesses production?

attributes.text: Disk encryption is enabled on every device that accesses production
attributes.typical_evidence: Per device command output or screenshot showing FileVault or BitLocker on, one per device in the inventory
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: For every device in the production-accessing inventory, actual command output or a screenshot of that output shows full disk encryption enabled (FileVault on, or BitLocker protection on and 100 percent encrypted). Evidence count matches the inventory. FAIL: Any inventoried device lacks encryption evidence, or any device shows encryption off or partial. NOTE: A founder-authored spreadsheet asserting encryption is not acceptable; the proof is the device's own command output or a screenshot of it.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Disk-encryption command output was captured for both founders' current laptops in the inventory, but a third, older laptop that was retired and removed from the device inventory before the test date has no capture.
calibration_examples.reasoning: Encryption evidence is measured against the current inventory, not a device already removed from service. A retired laptop no longer in the production-accessing inventory is outside the population, so full coverage of the two active inventoried devices passes.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A founder submits a short written statement asserting 'both our laptops have FileVault turned on' instead of an actual command output or screenshot from each device.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A founder-authored assertion is explicitly not acceptable proof for this attribute; the required evidence is the device's own command output or a screenshot of it. A typed claim with no real system capture gaps.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include actual disk encryption command output or a screenshot of it for each device in the inventory?
Does every device's output show full disk encryption enabled?

attributes.text: Screen lock is enabled on every device that accesses production
attributes.typical_evidence: Per device command output or screenshot showing password required after a short idle timeout, one per device in the inventory
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: For every device in the production-accessing inventory, command output or a screenshot shows screen lock enabled with a password required and an idle timeout of 15 minutes or less. Evidence count matches the inventory. FAIL: Any inventoried device lacks screen lock evidence, or shows screen lock disabled, or shows an idle timeout longer than 15 minutes. NOTE: The proof is the device's own setting output, not a verbal or written claim.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: Screenshots of each inventoried device's system settings show screen lock enabled with the timeout set to 'immediately,' rather than a specific minute count listed in a field.
calibration_examples.reasoning: An 'immediately' lock setting is strictly tighter than the 15-minute maximum the attribute allows, so the live capture plainly satisfies the requirement. No numeric minute value needs to appear separately when the setting is visibly within bound.

calibration_examples.evidence_summary: A founder describes in a Slack message that screen lock is enabled on all company devices, but no screenshots or command output from the devices themselves were captured.
calibration_examples.reasoning: A written or verbal assertion is never a substitute for the device's own setting output, which this attribute requires. Without an actual screenshot or command result per inventoried device, it gaps pending real evidence.

coverage_checks.question: Does the evidence include actual screen lock setting output or a screenshot of it for each device in the inventory?

attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: For every device in the production-accessing inventory, command output or a screenshot shows automatic operating system and software updates enabled.
